units.name: 1st Air Army
units.role: Fighter cover, tactical bombing and assault support from Orsha to Minsk, Vilnius and Kaunas.
units.locator: Opening deployment and four front operations

units.name: 3rd Air Army
units.role: Supported the northern pincer at Vitebsk and the subsequent advance toward Polotsk and Šiauliai.

units.name: 4th Air Army
units.role: Supported the Mogilev axis and the crossings on the route to the Dnieper.

units.name: 16th Air Army
units.role: Concentrated air support around Bobruisk, then operated toward Minsk and Baranovichi.

units.name: 6th Air Army
units.role: Supported the July offensive toward Lublin and the Vistula with attached units from the 16th Air Army and reserves.

units.name: Long-Range Aviation (ADD)
units.role: Supported the offensive with selected night missions and appears separately in the Mogilev preparation figures.

units.name: 4th Assault Aviation Corps
units.role: Assigned to attack troops and equipment inside the Bobruisk pocket.

units.name: GC 3 Normandie
units.role: French Yak fighter unit. Its journal follows an escort mission near Orsha and its memorial records a later transfer accident.

units.name: Luftflotte 6
units.role: Air fleet commanded by Robert Ritter von Greim. Headquarters moved from the Minsk area to Warsaw during the retreat.

units.name: I./JG 51
units.role: Bf 109 fighter Gruppe associated with Orsha. Station and strength publications disagree on the exact late-June position.

units.name: III./JG 51
units.role: Bf 109 fighter Gruppe based at Bobruisk in the opening battles and moved west after 27 June.

units.name: I./SG 10
units.role: Fw 190 ground-attack Gruppe at Bobruisk in the opening week.

units.name: 12./NAGr. 12
units.role: Short-range reconnaissance Staffel listed at Mogilev with Bf 109s.

units.name: II. and III./KG 4
units.role: He 111 bomber Gruppen listed at Baranovichi. Their presence is established in the listing, while a matching sortie series remains open.

units.name: 4. Flieger-Division
units.role: Luftflotte 6 command associated with Orsha. Tessin places its headquarters at Sudauen in July.

cases.title: Concentrating the air armies
cases.summary: Four fronts prepared a coordinated assault against Army Group Centre. Reserve formations reinforced the front air armies. The southern air plan assigned night bombing, reconnaissance and ground support by army sector.
cases.limit: Preparatory orders are dated before the offensive. The force snapshots shown here also include the first days of the operation. Their readiness definitions and populations differ.
cases.locator: 9 June plan, army and aviation tasks

cases.title: Mogilev and the Dnieper
cases.summary: Aircraft supported the 2nd Belorussian Front before its attack across the Pronya and on toward the Dnieper. The German 4th Army faced converging breakthroughs on its flanks and withdrew from the exposed bridgehead.
cases.limit: The two opening-night sortie counts belong to front aviation and Long-Range Aviation. The later 50th Army report has a catalogue reference. Its figures remain to be verified.

cases.title: Vitebsk and the Western Dvina
cases.summary: The 1st Baltic and 3rd Belorussian fronts converged on Vitebsk. The 3rd Air Army supported the river crossings and the encirclement. Its published history records a sharp rise in activity from 23 to 26 June.
cases.limit: The reported sorties cover the 3rd Air Army’s wider sector. Its victory claims have no matched German loss series here.

cases.title: Orsha and the rail corridor
cases.summary: The 1st Air Army massed much of its opening force on the Orsha axis. French pilots escorted a Pe-2 mission against Bogushevsk. German fighter listings and June movement returns give a second perspective on the sector.
cases.limit: The German listings and basing chronology differ for I./JG 51 around 26 June. The June removals cover the whole month.

cases.title: Bobruisk: claims and returns
cases.summary: The 16th Air Army supported both pincers around the German 9th Army. Its 26 June account gives sortie, loss and victory-claim figures. German returns show what two locally based Gruppen lost across the full month.
cases.limit: The 12 June enemy-action removals cap losses for those two Gruppen on any single June day. The 26 June Soviet claims cover a wider population.
cases.locator: Chapter 3, first three days of the offensive

cases.title: Bobruisk: the pocket strike
cases.point: Approximate pocket sector southeast of Bobruisk
cases.summary: On 27 June the 16th Air Army sent bombers, assault aircraft and fighters against the encircled force. Separate formations handled bombing, low-level attack and fighter patrol. Bobruisk fell on 29 June.
cases.limit: The air army reported zero own losses for the evening strike. The number applies to that mission only.

cases.title: Polotsk and the northern flank
cases.summary: The 1st Baltic Front cleared Polotsk while the 3rd Air Army attacked crossings and retreating traffic along the Dvina and Drissa. The advance widened the break between Army Groups Centre and North.
cases.limit: The 3rd Air Army’s 23–30 June figures include earlier Vitebsk operations. Polotsk’s own daily totals remain open.

cases.title: Berezina crossings and Minsk
cases.summary: Soviet aircraft attacked retreat roads and river crossings. Ziemke describes repeated attacks on the Berezino bridge as the German 4th Army staff withdrew. The pincers reached Minsk on 3 July as German aviation shifted west.
cases.limit: The bridge count is an account of attacks witnessed from the ground. The 1st Air Army’s aggregate spans 23 June to 3 July.
cases.locator: Chapter XV, Fourth Army diary and Minsk pocket

cases.title: Baranovichi airfields and rail junction
cases.summary: German forces resisted around the rail junction. Soviet fighters also attacked its airfield, and assault and night-bomber units hit roads, crossings and railway traffic. Baranovichi fell on 8 July.
cases.limit: German bomber stationing is a 26 June snapshot. It does not establish which bombers flew in the July battle.

cases.title: Vilnius and the Niemen approach
cases.summary: The 3rd Belorussian Front pursued the retreat through Vilnius. The 1st Air Army used reconnaissance to keep contact and continued support toward the Niemen. On 15 July a French Yak was lost in a transfer accident.
cases.limit: The 15 July accident is a named non-combat loss. Its map point represents the operation sector, with no claim about the accident coordinates.

cases.title: Šiauliai: range, fuel and forward fields
cases.summary: As ground troops outpaced the airfields, the 3rd Air Army described longer transits and fuel constraints. Fighters from the 1st Air Army helped cover the advance while the northern air units moved forward.
cases.limit: The Soviet history reports renewed German opposition. A daily German sortie or loss return has yet to be matched to this account.

cases.title: Lublin–Brest and the Vistula
cases.point: Brest sector, within the wider Lublin–Vistula operation
cases.summary: The 1st Belorussian Front’s left wing opened a new thrust with air support led by the 6th Air Army. Brest fell on 28 July and Soviet troops established Vistula bridgeheads.
cases.limit: The 6th Air Army sortie tally covers the left wing from 18–31 July. It includes activity beyond Brest itself.
cases.locator: Chapter 3, left wing and July totals

cases.title: Kaunas and the retreating fighter groups
cases.summary: The 1st Air Army supported the Kaunas operation. German records already place two Gruppen there earlier in July during their retreat from Belarus. Their dated basing and later operation chronology show different stages of the advance.
cases.limit: The basing windows precede the Kaunas battle. The markers indicate city sectors and station associations.
cases.locator: Kaunas operation and post-capture air reorganisation

cases.title: August: wider air operations and the campaign total
cases.summary: Air activity continued as the front widened. The 1st Air Army account records strikes on 16 August and support around Kelmė. The 3rd Air Army history describes continued airfield attacks in the Baltic sector.
cases.limit: The 822 figure is the Soviet strategic operation’s reported combat-aircraft loss total for 23 June–29 August. German Gruppen returns cover selected units and whole calendar months.
cases.locator: Equipment losses by strategic operation, Belorussian offensive row

cases.title: Osovets and the Narew approaches
cases.summary: The 2nd Belorussian Front continued from Białystok toward the Narew and took Osovets on 14 August. Published accounts associate Baydukov’s 4th Assault Aviation Corps with the preparatory bombardment.
cases.limit: The operation catalogue supports the ground chronology. The air attack attribution still needs the corps mission return, and sortie and loss counts remain open.
